scale: 1-5; 2 and 4 sit between the written anchors
title: Channel strategy (positioning, pillars, formats, calendar)

anchors.1: Opinions only; no real channels or posts examined.
anchors.3: Some real competitors with URLs; few measured numbers.
anchors.5: Built on examined competitors and posts with measured numbers and dates.

anchors.3: A clear niche, but a competitor could claim it.
anchors.5: A promise only this channel can keep; passes the swap test.

anchors.1: Pillars overlap or are topics, not repeatable formats.
anchors.5: 3–5 distinct pillars, each with a repeatable format, structure and production route.

anchors.1: Cadence or budget impossible for the team.
anchors.5: Cadence and cost proven or piloted; batch plan exists.

anchors.1: Ignores how the platform recommends content.
anchors.3: Mentions the algorithm in general terms.
anchors.5: Uses verified platform facts (dated) for packaging, cadence and format mix.
Metrics against own median, review cadence, a monetization path with thresholds.

vetoes: policy: plan relies on inauthentic or mass-produced content
